questions.question: Where was Aristotle born?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Aristotle was born in the city of Stagira in Chalkidiki.
Incorrect. Athens is where he studied at Plato's Academy and later founded his own school, but he was not born there.
Incorrect. Chalcis is where he fled to at the end of his life and where he died, but he was not born there.
Incorrect. Pella was the Macedonian capital where he later tutored Alexander, but he was not born there.

questions.question: At what age did Aristotle join Plato's Academy?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says he joined Plato's Academy at around eighteen years old.
Incorrect. The article does not mention this age for joining the Academy.
Incorrect. Thirty-seven is the age at which he left the Academy, not when he joined.
Incorrect. The article says he was around eighteen, not sixteen.

questions.question: Who did Aristotle tutor at the request of Philip II of Macedon?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that at the request of Philip II of Macedon, Aristotle tutored his son Alexander the Great.
Incorrect. Plato was Aristotle's own tutor, not someone Aristotle tutored.
Incorrect. Theophrastus was a colleague and successor, not a student of this kind.
Incorrect. Antipater was named as executor in Aristotle's will, not a student he tutored.

questions.question: What was the name of the school that Aristotle founded in Athens?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says he established his own school in a building known as the Lyceum.
Incorrect. The Academy was Plato's school, not Aristotle's.
Incorrect. The Stoa is not mentioned as a school founded by Aristotle.
Incorrect. The Museum is not mentioned as a school in this context.

questions.question: Which of these works is listed as one of Aristotle's most important treatises?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article lists Nicomachean Ethics among his most important treatises.
Incorrect. The Republic is a work by Plato, not Aristotle.
Incorrect. The Iliad is a poem by Homer, which Aristotle gifted to Alexander, but it is not his own treatise.
Incorrect. Organon is the name given to the collection of his logical works, but it is not listed as one of his most important treatises in that specific list.

questions.question: Why did Aristotle have to rent the Lyceum?
options: He was a metic and could not own property in Athens
He wanted to be close to the gymnasium
He was forced to by the Macedonian king
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that as a metic, Aristotle could not own property in Athens and thus rented the Lyceum.
Incorrect. While the Lyceum had a gymnasium, that is not the reason he rented it.
Incorrect. The article does not say he preferred renting; it says he could not own property.
Incorrect. There is no mention that the Macedonian king forced him to rent.

questions.question: What did Aristotle reportedly say when he fled Athens near the end of his life?
options: I will not allow the Athenians to sin twice against philosophy
The unexamined life is not worth living
I know that I know nothing
Give me a lever long enough and I will move the world
answer_explanations: Correct. The article quotes him as saying 'I will not allow the Athenians to sin twice against philosophy'.
Incorrect. This is a famous saying of Socrates, not Aristotle.
Incorrect. This is a saying attributed to Socrates, not Aristotle.
Incorrect. This is a saying attributed to Archimedes, not Aristotle.

questions.question: According to the article, what did Aristotle's father Nicomachus do?
options: He was the personal physician of King Amyntas of Macedon
He was a philosopher at Plato's Academy
He was a general in the Macedonian army
He was a merchant from Stagira
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Nicomachus was the personal physician of King Amyntas of Macedon.
Incorrect. There is no mention of Nicomachus being a philosopher at the Academy.
Incorrect. The article does not say he was a general.
Incorrect. The article does not describe him as a merchant.

questions.question: What did Aristotle do while he was at Assos with Theophrastus?
options: He did extensive research in botany and marine biology
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says that while at Assos, Aristotle and Theophrastus did extensive research in botany and marine biology.
Incorrect. The Nicomachean Ethics is believed to have been composed later, during his second period in Athens.
Incorrect. He tutored Alexander later, after leaving Assos.
Incorrect. He founded the Lyceum later, after returning to Athens.

questions.question: What happened to most of Aristotle's original writings?
options: Only around a third has survived
They were all destroyed in a fire
They were lost in a shipwreck
They were hidden and never found
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that only around a third of his original output has survived.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a fire destroying his writings.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a shipwreck.
Incorrect. Although some papers were hidden for protection, many copies circulated, and the article says a third survived, not that they were never found.
